summary: Board Camp Mountain lookout, Humboldt County: telephone line and lookout work in 1934, a volunteer lookout in 1953. FFLA lists the tower gone; no site description found.

facts.status_note: Listed as a tower that is gone; no source describes what remains.

events.note: Telephone line work began at Board Camp; the lookout was hoped to be ready for occupancy within two weeks
John S. Williamson, a volunteer known as Board Camp Johnny, had spent ten seasons at the lookout and made improvements
Six Rivers National Forest no longer considered it a key lookout point, though observations were still needed in critical fire weather

notes_for_editor: Two web searches found no page about this tower. The Weebly file name says broad-camp but the page heading reads BOARD CAMP; the story uses the page heading. The 1934 and 1953 items come through the Forest Lookouts page that quotes them, and the originals were not checked. No construction date, removal date or site description was found. The 1931 Blake Mountain clipping mentions Board Camp mountain only as a place on a telephone route, so it is not used as evidence of a lookout.
